page: Microsoft Azure E16-8ds_v6 is an x86_64 architecture server instance belonging to the Edsv6 family, running on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. It features a dedicated Intel Xeon 8573C processor with 4 physical cores and 8 vCPUs, operating at a clock speed of 4.2 GHz. The CPU includes 260 MB of L3 cache and supports advanced instruction sets such as AVX-512 and Intel Advanced Matrix Extensions (AMX). The instance is equipped with 128.0 GB of system memory, yielding a high memory-to-core ratio of 16.0 GB per core. Local storage is provided via a 945 GB NVMe SSD, and the instance does not include any GPUs or complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

In benchmark evaluations, the E16-8ds_v6 demonstrates strong single-threaded performance, notably achieving 31.38 GB/sec in gzip compression and a Geekbench single-core score of 2154.0. Text processing is also a strong point, scoring 2700.0 in Geekbench. Multi-core and general computational benchmarks, such as stress-ng multi-core (7989.66) and the Passmark CPU score (14249.49), fall within the average range. Memory performance is characterized by a cached read-only bandwidth of 621.15 GB/sec, while uncached large-block read and write bandwidths are 64.02 GB/sec and 43.34 GB/sec, respectively. For database workloads, the server handles 11.88 million Redis SET operations per second and scores 4990.18 in Passmark database operations.

The instance exhibits specific tradeoffs in machine learning workloads. While it shows strong performance in text generation for small LLM models (276.83 tokens/sec), its performance drops to weak levels for medium and large models, such as 8.24 tokens/sec for medium model text generation and 6.74 tokens/sec for large model prompt processing. This makes it less suitable for heavy AI inference tasks. However, the high memory density of 16.0 GB per core combined with fast local NVMe storage makes this instance highly cost-efficient for memory-intensive workloads that do not require massive parallel compute. It is well-suited for relational databases, in-memory caching systems like Redis, text processing pipelines, and general-purpose enterprise applications requiring a large memory footprint.

It features 128.0 GB of RAM, offering a high memory-to-core ratio of 16.0 GB per core, alongside a 945 GB local NVMe SSD. Operating on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor, this x86_64 instance delivers strong single-core performance, highlighted by a Geekbench single-core score of 2154.0 and 31.38 GB/sec in gzip compression. While multi-core and database benchmarks sit in the average tier, the server is highly efficient for memory-bound workloads. However, it shows performance tradeoffs in larger LLM inference tasks.
